readFirst: #1502, #1503 and #1504 shortened /evolution.html hard: two conflicting recoverable figures became one, and seven regions became one answer with a supporting layer. Each of those was a rewrite of the words around a number, which is exactly when a number quietly stops meaning what it meant. This file pins the four dimensions of the answer that survived, with the assumption behind each, so a fifth rewrite that moves one of them fails by name instead of shipping.
versionStamp: `fixtureVersion` is the ONLY stamp. There is no timestamp and no git sha here on purpose: both change on a re-run that changed nothing, so neither can tell a reader whether a value moved. Bump `fixtureVersion` when a pinned value or an assumption changes, and `attestationVersion` when the module's own contract does.
safety: Fully synthetic. Every figure is computed in-process from the bundled invented example dataset — no customer data, no credential, no network call, no live integration, and nothing read from a reader's browser. Nothing in this file is interpolated into HTML.
computedBy: …which is the same pair src/evolution-page.js calls to paint #finops-recoverable-attestation on /evolution.html. There is no second arithmetic path, here or on the page.
regenerate: node --input-type=module -e "import {loadExampleDataset} from './src/example-dataset.js'; import {recoverableAttestation} from './src/finops-answer-contract.js'; const a = recoverableAttestation(loadExampleDataset()); console.log(JSON.stringify({dimensions: a.dimensions, statement: a.statement}, null, 2));" — then copy `dimensions` into the four `value` fields below and `statement` into `statement`, and paste the same sentence into #finops-recoverable-attestation in src/evolution.html. Deterministic: the generator reads no clock and no random source, so a re-run reproduces these bytes exactly. tests/finops-consolidated-answer-attestation.test.js fails if any of the three copies disagree.

headline.assumption: The monthly sum over scored departments is the basis of record because it is the only recoverable figure derived from real per-department rows; the annual figure is a projection of it and is never quoted on its own. This is the reconciliation #1502 landed, and pinning the monthly figure is what stops a second annual constant reappearing beside it.

confidence.assumption: The band is the analysis envelope's own confidence signal ('Medium'), normalised through the published cut points — high at 75, medium at 50, low below — and not a second scale invented for this answer. A decimal here would read as a probability that the figure is correct, which nothing on this page measures.

provenance.assumption: A figure the export states survives a challenge from the person who exported it; a figure this page worked out must be defended on its rule instead, so the split is the provenance fact a disputing director needs first. Declared is CHECKED, not labelled: an operand counts as declared only when the envelope states that exact value itself, verified operand by operand on every call. 5 of 7 declared is the honest reading of this dataset — the period, the scope count, the analyzed total, the monthly recoverable line and the confidence band are the export's own; the scored-department count and the annual projection are ours.

coverage.assumption: A department is scored or it is not; there is no partial credit and nothing is ever extrapolated from the scored departments to the unscored ones. Both counts travel with the figure because a total over a subset that does not say so is a floor presented as a ceiling. 5 of 5 means this dataset supports the figure as an organisation total rather than a floor.

operandsNote: The full table, so the two provenance counts above can be audited rather than taken on trust. Each operand's own one-line assumption lives beside it in src/finops-answer-contract.js — ATTESTATION_OPERANDS — because that is where a reader changing one would be standing.
statement: Priced from the bundled example export's own usage records: 5 of the 7 inputs behind the figure above are stated by the export itself and 2 are worked out on this page, covering 5 of 5 departments in scope, over the most recent complete month. Medium confidence — enough to plan against, not yet enough to bill against. The How we know this note above names the version of this check, the pinned evidence file, and the assumption behind every input.
statementNote: The exact sentence #finops-recoverable-attestation carries on /evolution.html, authored in the served markup and repainted verbatim by src/finops-answer-contract-view.js. The page holds no number of its own: if the authored bytes and this string disagree, the page is wrong, not this file. THE HEADLINE IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THE SENTENCE. #finops-recoverable-answer states its one recoverable figure once and its annual projection once — tests/evolution.test.js holds it to exactly that — so restating $51,254 here would put back the competing figure #1496 and #1502 removed. The attested headline rides as the slot's `data-headline` attribute instead, which the drift check reads and no reader is shown twice. NOR ARE THE IDENTIFIERS, SINCE #1554. The sentence answers one executive question — what is the figure priced from, and how sure are we — in words a reader who has never opened this repository can repeat, so the attestation version, this fixture's path and the operand codes are stated in the Provenance part of #finops-recoverable-how-we-know instead of in the sentence. Nothing was dropped: the version is also still on the slot's `data-version`, the counts on `data-declared` / `data-derived` / `data-scored` / `data-in-scope`, and src/finops-executive-vocabulary.js is the one mapping from each identifier to the phrase that replaced it. tests/finops-executive-vocabulary.test.js fails the sentence, in the served bytes and in the paint, if any forbidden token shape returns to it.
